Yeah! ROCm 10 is running on my RX 6700 XT! Created an Ubuntu 26.04 chroot for ROCm 10 on m…
news.author: sheepfreak@pixelfed.social
news.snippet: Yeah! ROCm 10 is running on my RX 6700 XT! Created an Ubuntu 26.04 chroot for ROCm 10 on my Debian Testing system. First, I set up the AMD source list and tried to install ROCm directly from the AMD repository. I deliberately chose Ubuntu 26.04 as the target system for ROCm, since it is one of the distributions officially supported by AMD's ROCm packages. Problem: The ROCm 10 packages required dependencies that no longer match Ubuntu 26.04 and its current GCC/libstdc++ version. AMD's amdrocm-llvm10.0 required libstdc++-14-dev or older, while Ubuntu 26.04 offered libstdc++-15-dev instead. I suspect AMD packaged the packages with dependencies for an older GCC/libstdc++ version. So, plan B: TheRock I downloaded a suitable TheRock tarball for gfx103X, extracted it and added the ROCm userspace to my PATH. rocminfo detects my RX 6700 XT. I originally wanted to use my ROCm test script from my current ROCm 7 chroot, but that would have meant downloading several GB of PyTorch for ROCm 10 and I did not feel like doing that xD So instead, I compiled a small HIP kernel with hipcc, explicitly targeting gfx1031, and executed it on the RX 6700 XT. After removing an environment variable that was incorrectly forcing the GPU to be reported as gfx1030, the kernel ran successfully. I then ran a vector addition test and a small FP32 compute benchmark. And it runs! I do not know if or when I will migrate from ROCm 7 to ROCm 10. My AI stack is already extremely stable and never change a running system! And I also have no idea how long RDNA2 will be able to handle the new models! #ROCm #ROCm10 #AMD #Radeon #RX6700XT #RDNA2 #HIP #AMDGPU #TheRock #Linux #LinuxDesktop #Debian #Ubuntu #FOSS #OpenSource #AI #ArtificialIntelligence #LocalAI #OpenSourceAI #MachineLearning #DeepLearning #GPUComputing #GPU #GPUAcceleration #Compute #HPC #Tech #RadeonGPU

tech.snippet: Self-hostable workflow orchestrator for teams whose main work isn't orchestration.
